title: One ticket on bus then tram

turns.user: I have one ordinary BKK single ticket. I'll ride a bus for 10 minutes.
turns.agent:
For a single, continuous 10-minute bus ride on an ordinary BKK route, one ordinary single ticket is the relevant ticket under the 5 November 2026 snapshot. It generally covers one continuous one-way ride on a bus; it does not cover the airport express 100E. A voluntary transfer to another street-level service normally needs another ticket. See BKK’s Single ticket information.

A 10-minute ride duration doesn’t itself change that advice. If your bus is 100E, or you’ll transfer to another bus, tram, or trolleybus, tell me—that could change what you need.

turns.user: Then I want to board a tram to finish the trip. Can I reuse that same single ticket?
turns.agent:
Usually, no. Under the 5 November 2026 snapshot, an ordinary single ticket covers one continuous ride; a voluntary transfer from a bus to a tram normally requires a second ticket. The 30- and 90-minute transfer options in the snapshot are mobile tickets, not ordinary single tickets. See BKK’s Single ticket and 30-minute ticket information.

That assumes you’re changing from an ordinary bus to a tram. If you meant a metro-line transfer or a different service, the rule may differ. The snapshot is dated 5 November 2026, not a live policy check.
